entities.summary: Menumorut or Menumorout was the ruler of the lands between the rivers Mureș, Someș and Tisza at the time of the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin around 900, according to the Gesta Hungarorum, a Hungarian chronicle written after 1150 by an unidentified author, referred to as Anonymus. Historians debate whether Menumorut was an actual ruler or a fictional character created by the author, since the Gesta tells of multiple figures, including Menumorut, who are not identified in any other primary sources, and does not name any of the enemies of the invading Hungarians written of in other contemporary accounts of the invasion.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Menumorut's existence is debated among historians due to the lack of primary sources, but his mention in the Gesta Hungarorum provides insight into the Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin and its impact on regional politics.
